title: Random Matrix Diagnostics of Endogenous Correlations
research_question: Do spectral patterns of model-generated financial returns identify economically meaningful common risk beyond sampling noise?
feasibility_hypothesis: Direct as a statistical diagnostic of equilibrium outcomes, but random matrix theory by itself is not an optimal-choice or market-clearing mechanism.
mechanisms: Cross-asset covariance and spectral eigenvalue distributions
Marchenko-Pastur null when its assumptions hold
required_equations: Null distribution under documented independence assumptions
Model-generated covariance and risk network functions
comparison_baseline: Independent asset returns and conventional factor models at the same sample size
acceptance_tests: Recover reference null with controlled Monte Carlo
Stability under heavy tails and time dependence
Link risk eigenvectors back to holdings and balance sheets
Do not mistake statistical significance for a new equilibrium mechanism
stage_gate: Retain only diagnostically or predictively informative spectral statistics; no artificial structural claim.

implementation.method: equilibrium solving plus ABM/distribution verification when relevant
implementation.language: Julia proposed; environment and APIs to be verified before implementation
